subject: Operator certification, runbook & training requirements for on‑prem deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@orthogen.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Operator certification and runbook — initial questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Orthogen's procurement and security review for a private (VPC / air‑gapped) deployment we have several follow‑ups specifically around on‑site operator responsibilities, training expectations, and runbook content. Can you confirm the following (high level answers are fine for now):

1) Operator certification: Do you provide a formal certification or acceptance matrix for customer operators (e.g., checklist-based signoff that an operator completed training and a hands‑on verification)? If so, what does it cover and how long is certification valid?

2) Runbook scope: Please list the major sections you include in an on‑prem runbook. We need to know whether it includes: installation validation, daily health checks, KV cache management, emergency rollback steps, airgap patch procedure, backup/restore, operator privileges, and escalation paths.

3) Training delivery: Do you run instructor-led on‑site training, remote live workshops, or self‑paced modules? How long are typical sessions and what materials do you hand over (slides, lab exercises, access tokens, test scripts)?

4) Acceptance criteria: For our internal compliance, we need pass/fail criteria for operator competence (e.g., complete N labs + runbook walk‑through + instructor signoff). Can you outline the criteria you recommend?

5) Patch maintenance in air‑gapped mode: Describe how patches are staged and validated for air‑gapped customers. Who signs off the SBOM and chain-of-custody for the patch bundle?

We have an internal milestone the week of Jun 21 — ideally we need a draft runbook and training outline by Jun 18 so our Security & Ops team can review. Can you confirm feasibility and any blockers?

Attachments: None

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kim
Lead, Cloud Security & Ops
Orthogen Therapeutics

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@orthogen.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator certification and runbook — initial questions

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear list. We can meet your Jun 18 target for a draft bundle. High‑level answers inline below; I'll follow up with a short packet (runbook + training outline + SOP excerpt). Rishi (serving runtime lead) and Jordan (solutions lead) are looped in for technical and scheduling details.

1) Operator certification: Yes — we maintain a certification checklist we use for customer operators. It covers: environment prep, deployment verification, restart/rollback procedures, cache invalidation, safe re‑quantization procedures, and disaster recovery drills. Certification is valid for 12 months; recertification is recommended after major version upgrades.

2) Runbook scope: Typical top‑level sections we include:
- Preflight and environment checklist (network, KMS, hardware inventory)
- Installation & image verification (checksums, SBOM mapping)
- Daily/weekly health checks & KPIs (latency, queue depth, batch rates)
- Operator tasks (start/stop, cache flush, key rotation, failover)
- Incident response & rollback playbook (including canary failover)
- Air‑gapped patching & validation workflow
- Backup/restore and KV cache persistence
- Escalation contacts & maintainability notes

3) Training delivery: We offer a 2‑day instructor‑led workshop (remote or on‑site) plus a one‑day hands‑on lab. Materials: slide deck, lab guide with scripted exercises, sample anonymized test dataset, and an operator checklist. We can also provide a self‑paced lab environment for certification practice.

4) Acceptance criteria: Recommended matrix: complete 6 labs (deployment, restart, restore, patch apply, rollback, emergency failover) with >=80% checklist items validated; plus one runbook walk‑through demo to an instructor; and an instructor signoff form. We can adapt criteria to Orthogen's compliance needs.

5) Patch maintenance air‑gapped: We produce signed patch bundles with SBOM and cryptographic signatures. Customer security retains control of install; Redwood provides verification artifacts and a verification playbook. For air‑gapped installs, either customer signs off on the chain‑of‑custody or we can work under an authorized courier model.

Feasibility: No blockers from our side. We'll attach the draft runbook (v1.2), training outline, and a short SOP excerpt on air‑gap patching by Jun 18. Can you provide: preferred time windows for training (week of Jun 28) and a contact at Security for SBOM handshake?

Attachments: [placeholder — draft packet will be sent Jun 18]

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick reply, that looks promising. A couple of clarifications from Security: 

- For the certification matrix can you provide a template signoff form (we need fields for trainee name, operator ID, lab scores, instructor signature, date)?
- For air‑gap SBOM verification we will want a hash and signature verification step documented that our SRE can run; can you include sample commands or a validation script in the runbook appendix?
- For the courier model, please outline expected timelines for packaging, signatures, and a recommended chain‑of‑custody form.

Timelines: Jun 18 draft is critical for our internal milestone. If you can also include a one‑pager that maps runbook sections to our control IDs (we can share control IDs privately), that would speed reviews.

Security contact for SBOM handshake:
- Maya Sandoval <m.sandoval@orthogen.com> (cc'd to security alias)

Appreciate it — we look forward to the draft packet.

Regards,
Daniel

Attached is the draft packet ahead of your Jun 21 milestone. Included: runbook v1.2 (PDF), operator training outline (PDF), and an SOP excerpt for air‑gapped patch handling (DOCX). Key notes up front:

- Runbook v1.2 highlights: added a Runbook Acceptance checklist (Appendix C) and a short validation script (Appendix D) for SBOM/hash verification. The daily checks map to typical latency and KV cache KPIs; incident rollback is a 3‑step canary failover with explicit operator commands.
- Training outline: 2‑day agenda (Day 1: architecture + deployment labs; Day 2: incident simulation + patch exercise) and a certification checklist. The certification template is included as a fillable form in Appendix B.
- Air‑gap SOP: lists packaging checklist, signature process, and recommended chain‑of‑custody form — expected courier timeline is 3–5 business days from signoff.

Next steps we propose:
1) Security review of Appendix D (validation script) — please flag any commands that need to be adjusted for your hardened environment.
2) Confirm training week preference (we recommended Jun 28 but can shift).
3) Provide your control ID mapping doc (we'll map runbook sections to your controls and return a mapped one‑pager).
